notes: Audio generation feature: chapter-level Edge TTS narration for a FIXED allowlist.

ClipForge is the reference TTS implementation. Ported verbatim from pipeline/stage_b/voiceover.py (curated Edge neural catalog, 3-attempt retry with linear backoff, two-pass EBU R128 loudnorm speech_clarity_v1 chain, 24kHz mono s16le WAV internal contract).
VerseWell overrides: rate=+0% (calm long-form pace, NOT ClipForge's +20% brisk), MP3 96 kbps mono 24 kHz final for repo storage.

task-02 verified DONE prior to this session: voice.sqlite3 is already inside /bible-sources/ and no /bible-sources-staging/ directory exists — the earlier static-only migration commit '064e7771 static-only task-03/04: move voice.sqlite3 into /bible-sources/, remove staging' handled it.

versewell_narration_overrides.rate_rationale: Calm, natural Scripture-reading pace. ClipForge's +20% is tuned for short-video brisk narration; long-form reading needs comfortable intelligibility over energy. +0% chosen after weighing that a slight -3%/-5% slowdown risked sounding sluggish on longer chapters (Ps 119, Isa 1) with no clarity gain over +0% Edge neural voices, which are already deliberately paced.
versewell_narration_overrides.output_format_rationale: MP3 96 kbps mono 24 kHz balances intelligibility with repo storage. Raw WAV per chapter (~1.5 MB/min) would push the whole allowlist >40 GB; MP3 keeps it within acceptable git bounds (~11 GB estimate) while remaining above transparency threshold for spoken voice.

audio_enabled_versions_captured_from: site/static-data/index.json version codes on 2026-09-07 after confirming /bible-sources/ contains: amp.sqlite3, cev.sqlite3, gw.sqlite3, kjv.sqlite3, msg.sqlite3, niv2011.sqlite3, nkjv.sqlite3, nlt.sqlite3, nlv.sqlite3, tlb.sqlite3, tpt.sqlite3, voice.sqlite3. Note: niv2011.sqlite3 is served under code NIV (per importer normalization) so 'NIV' is the correct allowlist token, not 'NIV2011'.
audio_enabled_versions_policy: CLOSED, PERMANENT ALLOWLIST. Any version added to /bible-sources/ after 2026-09-07 must NEVER automatically receive audio. scripts/generate_audio.py enforces this at runtime; a new version silently absent from AUDIO_STATE.json.audio_enabled_versions is a no-op for audio.

voice_assignment.algorithm: Sort audio_enabled_versions alphabetically. Assign voices in order, alternating Male, Female, Male, Female, .... Only calm 'narrator' or 'conversational-style' Edge neural voices; ClipForge's energetic 'Guy' and casual 'Brian' explicitly excluded.

table.style: Calm British narrator, fits KJV Anglo heritage

audio_storage_layout: site/static-data/{version_lower}/{book_slug}/{chapter}.mp3 (colocated with the existing per-chapter JSON, so Pages serves both from one deploy and the chapter JSON can reference a same-directory sibling).
audio_url_field_shape: In each chapter JSON: audio_url = '/static-data/{version_lower}/{book_slug}/{chapter}.mp3' if the file exists, else null. Non-allowlisted versions ALWAYS emit null.

generation_workflow.trigger: workflow_dispatch ONLY (never on push; audio generation is expensive)
generation_workflow.idempotency: scripts/generate_audio.py --skip-existing: any chapter whose target .mp3 already exists is skipped. Re-runs pick up interrupted work with no duplication.
generation_workflow.budget_control: workflow inputs 'max_chapters' and 'versions' let an operator do partial runs; unset = 'as many as fit in the 6h Actions job budget'.
generation_workflow.auto_resume: 2026-09-08: each run is a 6h 'slice'. If chapters remain unfinished it re-dispatches itself (gh workflow run, inputs resume=cleanup=on, auto=1) using the AUDIO_RESUME_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT, actions:write). Chain repeats until the render completes. Without the secret the chain stops with a warning and the operator re-triggers manually.
generation_workflow.self_cleanup: When a resume-chain run (auto=1) finds 0 chapters remaining it refreshes audio_url fields, then git-rms .github/workflows/generate-audio.yml and scripts/generate_audio.py, commits and pushes — deleting all audio GENERATION artifacts from main while keeping the rendered .mp3 files and the audio_url JSON. A manual dispatch (auto != 1) never self-deletes.
